questions.stem: All of the following features of nephrotic syndrome except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Hematuria
  • Hematuria is not a feature of nephrotic syndrome. It is typically seen in glomerular diseases that involve inflammation or damage to the glomerular capillaries, such as IgA nephropathy, lupus nephritis, or rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis.
  • However, it is not a common feature of nephrotic syndrome, which is primarily characterized by proteinuria and hypoalbuminemia.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 914

questions.stem: The hypercoagulable state in nephrotic syndrome is due to:
questions.solutionHtml:
Loss of antithrombin III
  • The hypercoagulable state in nephrotic syndrome is primarily due to the loss of antithrombin III.
  • This loss is due to increased urinary excretion and decreased hepatic synthesis of antithrombin III.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 914
